unit.title: Field Kit: The Lorekeeper Workbench
unit.pitch: Try every interactive lesson format in one small workbench before choosing a full course.

blocks.prompt: A customer reports that the booking page is down. Put the first response in a safe order. Use the up and down buttons, then check.
blocks.explanation: Evidence first, then contain, eradicate, recover and review. Restoring before containing can destroy the evidence and repeat the outage.

blocks.prompt: Fill the blanks with the viewport setting, a useful image description and the right input type.

answers: The timber counter and display cabinet at the Northbridge store
The counter and display cabinet at the Northbridge store
blanks.hint: Describe what the image shows, not that it is an image.
Use the input type made for email addresses.

blocks.prompt: Click the three things that should not be public on this small site.

targets.label: Public user endpoint
targets.feedback: Account names help an attacker. Restrict or disable it.

targets.label: Old administrator account
targets.feedback: An unowned administrator is a way in. Remove it.

targets.label: Menu PDF
targets.feedback: A PDF does not reflow on a phone. Replace it with HTML.

blocks.prompt: This commit made a failing check pass. Click the lines that hid the problem instead of fixing the page.

lines.feedback: A comment cannot make a broken page work.

blocks.explanation: The page was not fixed. The check was weakened. Revert the check and fix the layout.

blocks.prompt: The client needs staff editing, online bookings and a small three-year budget. Choose the path you would recommend.

options.label: WordPress agency
options.outcome: Dev can edit the menu and hours. Hosting and updates cost money. The exit cost is medium.
options.feedback: This matches the staff-editing priority and keeps the exit cost moderate.

options.label: AI site builder
options.outcome: Fast to start. Dev cannot change the content model. Moving later means rebuilding the site.

options.label: Custom rebuild from scratch
options.outcome: Full control. The client pays for everything twice and needs a developer on call.
options.feedback: The budget does not support a custom build and its maintenance.

blocks.debrief: The cheapest quote is not the lowest three-year cost. The board is buying an outcome, not a build.

blocks.prompt: Read both critiques of the same site, choose the stronger one, and write one sentence about why.

a.title: Critique A
a.body: The site has ten problems. The font is inconsistent, the footer is crowded, the colours are uneven, the images are different sizes, the menu is a PDF, the booking form is long, the about page is thin, the headings skip a level, the alt text is poor, and the domain is owned by the old developer.

b.title: Critique B
b.body: I would not charge yet. The menu is a PDF, so the main customer task fails on a phone. The booking form takes four taps, and the domain is still in the previous developer's name. I would fix the menu, shorten the booking flow and transfer the domain before launch.

blocks.rationale: Critique B chooses, prioritises and ties each point to a customer task. Critique A lists everything and leaves the decision to the client.

blocks.context: You recommended WordPress over an AI site builder. The examiner is non-technical but has read both proposals.

questions.prompt: Why not the AI builder? It is half the price.
questions.strong_answer: It is half the build price, not half the three-year cost. Dev cannot edit the content model, and leaving the platform would mean rebuilding the site. The agency costs more now and less to leave.

Keep WordPress and the content model. Drop the custom booking flow for the first six months and use a form with a manual process. Protect the handover and the editing experience before the automation.

rubric: Recommendation reasoning holds up under challenge.
The answer adapts when the brief changes.
The language works for a non-technical board.

blocks.prompt: Send each request and read the response. Then answer the exposure questions.

questions.prompt: Which endpoint exposes account names to an anonymous request?
questions.explanation: The users endpoint lists accounts. Restrict it.

questions.prompt: Which endpoint contains customer personal data?
questions.explanation: Names and phone numbers are personal data. Authenticate it or keep it server-only.

questions.prompt: What should happen to the users endpoint?
questions.explanation: Public account lists help enumeration. Close it unless there is a reason to keep it.

blocks.prompt: Run a query against the menu database. The result must match the task.
blocks.task: List the name and price of every available item, cheapest first.
blocks.seed:
INSERT INTO menu_items (name, price, available) VALUES
  ('Sourdough', 8.0, 1),
  ('Croissant', 6.0, 1),
  ('Flat white', 5.0, 0),
  ('Rye loaf', 9.0, 1);
blocks.solution:
SELECT name, price
FROM menu_items
WHERE available = 1
ORDER BY price ASC;
